we present the design and realization of a multilayer LTCC solution for the integration of 5G access point antenna modules.

the design of a new class of LTCC-based multilayer antenna structures for 5G applications.

the design, implementation and testing of multilayer low temperature cofired ceramics (LTCC) solutions for the development of millimetre-wave antenna modules for fifth generation (5G) communication systems.
the design of a novel LTCC multilayer antenna module that can be integrated with a 5G baseband unit (BBU) for the V-band (60 GHz).

a novel implementation of a full-coprporate feed network (CFM), exploiting the 3-D capabilities of the LTTC process and employing dielectric- embedded parallel plate waveguidelines (PPWs) has been proposed.
the proposed multilayer LTCC solution for integrating 5G access point antenna modules is a viable option for the future V-band wireless networks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed the first LTCC-based 5G antenna solution, and the first 5G antenna prototype that can operate in the 5G band, which is the most challenging part of the 5G frequency band, i.e., the 50-60 GHz band, which is also the most important band of 5G.
we have demonstrated the first LTCC-based 5G access point module with multilayer feed network, which is capable to generate multibeam radiation patterns.
we developed a multilayer LTCC technology for the integration of millimeter wave antennas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multilayer LTCC technology can be used to integrate 5G access point antenna modules, with a compact size, high gain, and low cost.

the multilayer LTCC technology, with its 3-D integration potential, can be a viable solution for the realization of compact, high-performance, multilayer antenna structures, with a reduced number of layers, and without the use of complex assembly processes.
the proposed LTCC-based multilayer solution can be a cost-effective alternative to other technologies for 5G antenna integration.
